sentence.text: Ajrakh activities prevailed at Dhamadka for the past 450 years because of a water source from a stream of the Indus river; this stream dried up in 1989.

citations.quote: The Ajrakh activities prevailed at Dhamadka since the past 450 years, as it was having a potential water source from one of the water stream of the Indus river.
citations.locator: GI Journal No. 188 copy (application 1050), PDF p. 3

citations.quote: This water stream dried up in 1989 and water levels from wells and tanks continued to fall.
citations.locator: GI Journal No. 188 copy (application 1050), PDF p. 3

sentence.text: The river Saran in Dhamadka dried up by 1989, largely because bore pumps diverted water toward the Kandla Free Trade Zone.

citations.quote: In Dhamadka, the river Saran was always flowing, but it died a slow death by 1989. This was largely due to the increase in bore pumps which diverted the water towards the Kandla Free Trade Zone.
citations.locator: § "We are running out of water"

sentence.text: After the 2001 earthquake about a hundred families moved from Dhamadka to their present location 40 km away, in search of good quality groundwater.

citations.quote: Last time something like this had happened, the entire village of a hundred families moved from their earlier settlement in Dhamadka to their present location, 40 km away, in search of good quality groundwater. This transition was after the devastating earthquake in 2001 .
citations.locator: § "History repeats itself"

sentence.text: Excess iron in groundwater threatened Ajrakh in Dhamadka and is again threatening it in Ajrakhpur.

citations.quote: Excess iron in groundwater that threatened Ajrakh in Dhamadka, is once again threatening the craft in Ajrakhpur.
citations.locator: § "Share this article"

sentence.text: Indigo can be natural (Indigofera tinctoria) or synthetic 'German' indigo; natural indigo is fermented with lime, dates and soda; synthetic indigo often has 'Hydros' added.

citations.quote: Natural Indigo is purchased in blocks or cakes, ground to a powder and soaked before fermenting in an underground vat consisting strong alkaline lime powder, dates and carbonate of soda, plus specialty ingredients unique to each particular dyer.
citations.locator: GI Journal No. 188 copy (application 1050), PDF p. 7

sentence.text: Indigo is not soluble in water whereas leucoindigo is; indigo is transformed to leucoindigo by indigo-reducing bacteria.

citations.locator: § "Introduction"

sentence.text: Indigo is reduced to soluble 'indigo white' for dyeing and fixed to the fibre by air oxidation.

citations.quote: On oxidisation, indigo white is converted into granules of indigo blue which has then to be reduced through fermentation into soluble indigo white, before dyeing can begin.
citations.locator: § "Dyeing cotton fabrics is an ancient Indian art"

citations.quote: At first bright green, the cloth rapidly becomes blue as oxygen meets the dye particles on the fibres.

take.text: Rao Bharmalji I (1586-1631) invited Khatri printers from Sindh and gave them land and tax exemptions.

citations.quote: The erstwhile ruler of Kutch Rao Bharmalji - I (1586-1631), invited the cloth-printing Khatri artisans from Sindh and gave them permission to settle and earn their livelihoods anywhere in Kutch. They were given land by the state as well spared any taxation on their produce.
citations.locator: § "Mushtak Khan"

thisView.text: The technique came to Kutch from Sindh some 400 years ago at the behest of the King of Kutch, who invited Khatri craftsmen to the banks of the Dhamadka river.

citations.quote: This intricate and exclusively handcrafted block-printing technique came to Kutch from Sindh some 400 years ago at the behest of the King of Kutch, who invited craftsmen from Khatri community to come and practice their art on the banks of Dhamadka river.
citations.locator: GI Journal No. 188 copy (application 1050), PDF p. 9

citations.quote: During the 7th century, the Khatris of Sindh were Hindu. It is said that Sindh was invaded by Arabs and forced the people to convert to Islam. Those who converted stayed in Sindh. Those who refused fled to modern-day Kachchh.

citations.quote: Among them was Jinda Jeeva, our ancestor who came here in 1650.

take.text: Khatris made cloth for Maldharis and farming communities, often trading cloth for produce, milk or ghee; designs were not interchangeable between communities.

citations.quote: They produced cloth for maldharis (cattle herders), both Hindus and Muslims as well as farming communities across Kachchh. They used the barter system and exchanged cloth for produce from farmers, while cattle herders gave them milk or ghee.
